title: The people gather to consult
summary: Ammon and King Limhi consult with the gathered people about escaping bondage and seek the voice of the people.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and King Limhi consult with the people about how to escape bondage.
They cause all the people to gather to express their voice on the matter.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathered assembly is consulting together.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, arrangement, clothing, and appearance of the assembly are not specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific escape plan as already chosen.

title: No way by force
summary: The people can find no way out of bondage except to take their families and possessions into the wilderness; the Lamanites are too numerous to overcome by the sword.

explicit_facts.text: The people can find no way to escape bondage except by taking their families, flocks, herds, and tents and departing into the wilderness.
The Lamanites are too numerous for the people of Limhi to contend with by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people are considering flight rather than fighting.
unspecified_visual_details: No battle or departure is narrated here; the place where they consider their options is unspecified.

narration.text: it was impossible for the people of Limhi to contend with them

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a battle as occurring in this scene.

title: Gideon stands before the king
summary: Gideon goes forth and stands before the king. The king grants him permission to speak.

explicit_facts.text: Gideon goes forth and stands before the king.
Gideon recalls that the king has listened to his words during contention with the Lamanites.
Gideon asks the king to listen and promises to serve him and deliver the people out of bondage.
The king grants Gideon permission to speak.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gideon and the king are within speaking distance.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, physical appearances, and surrounding furnishings are unspecified.
The king's posture and manner of granting permission are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: even so I desire that thou wouldst listen to my words at this time, and I will be thy servant and deliver this people out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Gideon

narration.text: Now it came to pass that Gideon went forth and stood before the king, and said unto him:
And the king granted unto him that he might speak.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The dialogue is a selected exact excerpt, not the complete speech in verses 3–4.
Earlier contention is recalled, not enacted here. Deliverance is promised, not accomplished in these verses.
Verse 5 introduces further speech but supplies none of its words.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the king or invent his dialogue.
Do not add a deliverance plan or depict deliverance occurring.
Do not depict the earlier contention with the Lamanites as occurring in this scene.
Do not assume the Lamanites or the people mentioned are physically present.
Do not add the speech introduced but not supplied in verse 5.

title: A proposed route through the back pass
summary: A speaker proposes gathering livestock, paying a last tribute of wine, and departing with women and children through a secret pass into the wilderness, traveling around the land of Shilom.
characters: Speaker not named in the supplied verses

explicit_facts.text: The speaker describes a back pass through the back wall on the back side of the city and states that the Lamanites, or their guards, are drunken by night.
The speaker proposes sending a proclamation for the people to gather their flocks and herds to drive into the wilderness by night.
The speaker proposes paying the last tribute of wine according to the addressee's command and passing through the secret pass on the left of the Lamanite camp when they are drunken and asleep.
The proposed departure includes women, children, flocks, and herds, with travel into the wilderness around the land of Shilom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown explaining the proposal without depicting its execution.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's name, appearance, clothing, and gestures are not supplied.
The speech's location, time of day, and audience composition are unspecified.
The physical designs of the wall, pass, and camp are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the back pass, through the back wall, on the back side of the city.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Speaker not named in the supplied verses

spoken_dialogue.text: Thus we will depart with our women and our children, our flocks, and our herds into the wilderness; and we will travel around the land of Shilom.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Speaker not named in the supplied verses

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses present a proposal, not its execution.
The audit identifies Gideon using verse 5, but that verse is outside the permitted source. The supplied verses 6–8 do not name the speaker.
The summary describes the supplied speech event; it is not spoken narration.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as Gideon based on the audit's reference to an excluded verse.
Do not depict the proclamation, tribute delivery, drinking, sleep, livestock gathering, or escape as occurring during this speech.
Do not assume that women, children, livestock, or Lamanite guards are physically present at the speech.
Do not invent dialogue, the addressee's identity, or a visible route demonstration.

title: Wine is sent to the Lamanites
summary: Limhi gathers his people’s flocks and sends the Lamanites their wine tribute and additional wine as a present. They drink freely.

summary: At night, Limhi’s people depart into the wilderness with their flocks and herds, travel around Shilom, and head toward Zarahemla led by Ammon and his brethren.

title: The Lamanites pursue
summary: After discovering that Limhi’s people have left by night, the Lamanites send an army into the wilderness. After two days, the army loses the trail and is lost.
